preamble: Monophthongization of the rising diphthong [jɛ] to the open-mid vowel [ɛ]. The atlas symbol ie covers the diphthong in both its falling [ie] and rising [je]/[jɛ] realizations; the Italian input here is the rising [jɛ] with an open second element. In Florentine Tuscan, the [jɛ] that came from Latin stressed Ĕ in open syllables was reduced to [ɛ] after a consonant + r cluster around the middle of the 15th century, so that older prièga, prième, trièma gave modern standard Italian prèga, prème, trèma. The parallel reduction of [wɔ] to [ɔ] in the same context (pruòva > pròva, truòva > tròva) followed in the 16th century.
sources: Università degli Studi di Cagliari, Linguistica 2 (2020). Dal dittongo al monottongo. Riduzione /jɛ/ > /ɛ/ e riduzione /wɔ/ > /ɔ/. https://web.unica.it/static/resources/cms/documents/Linguistica2.Daldittongoalmonottongo.pdf
